name: Provident Brassie Data Center
summary: Provident withdrew its former Brassie Golf Course data-center proposal after resident opposition and the Town Council declared the scale and location unacceptable. Subsequent planning shifted toward other development concepts.
proposal_description: Provident proposed eight large data-center buildings and related generator, switching, and substation areas on and near the former Brassie Golf Course property.
site_afterlife: Town records in 2025 describe the development team shifting away from a data center and soliciting community input on a future development opportunity. The final alternative use is not yet fixed in this release.
evidence_note: The developer withdrawal and council position are primary-record facts. The site is classified as redesigned because development planning continued after the data-center concept ended.
unresolved_questions: Which portions of the former Brassie site remain under Provident's control?
Will the 2026 residential concept receive formal approval, and what final unit count and infrastructure commitments will it carry?
Were any data-center utility or tax-abatement negotiations completed before withdrawal?
What portion of post-2024 county change is observable at the town rather than county level?

timeline.title: Plan Commission receives the large-campus concept
timeline.summary: Provident presented a multi-building data-center concept for the former golf-course property.

timeline.title: Eight-building, $1.3 billion concept becomes public
timeline.summary: Trade reporting described eight roughly 150,000-square-foot buildings on about 200 acres, with a then-targeted 2026 opening.

timeline.title: Town Council rejects the proposal's scale and location
timeline.summary: The council said it could not support the project at its current scale and location and required extensive further review if pursued.

timeline.title: Provident formally withdraws both petitions
timeline.summary: The developer withdrew the planned-unit-development and annexation petitions.

timeline.title: Town solicits input on a different development opportunity
timeline.summary: The former Brassie property remained in planning, so the case is tracked as a redesign rather than permanent nondevelopment.

timeline.title: Residential replacement concept draws a new round of review
timeline.summary: Commission minutes record public discussion of a 632-unit concept and concerns involving traffic, sewage, stormwater, density, and schools.

timeline.title: Competing green-space concept enters the public record
timeline.summary: Town minutes document a separate Band of Builders concept, illustrating that future use of the former course remained unsettled.

timeline.title: Revised 501-unit concept advances to formal review
timeline.summary: Town notice traces the residential alternative from 604 units in 2025 to 501 units in February 2026 and schedules formal concept review.

county_outcome_context.note: The Porter County panel ends in the 2024 withdrawal year, so no complete post-decision year is available. Later residential concepts are parcel-level afterlife evidence, not evidence of countywide economic effects.
